name: Columbia Blue
lede: Columbia Blue is a pale blue Wikipedia credits to Columbia University, with a close hue already on Robert Ridgway's 1912 color plates.

sections.title: A paler cousin of Carolina Blue
sections.body:
Wikipedia credits Columbia University as the source of this name, and that is the only record of the naming itself in our sources [1]. Robert Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature carries a close hue on plate XXXIV, and the ISCC-NBS system later classified this chip as a very pale blue, about 2.2 units from that block's reference color [2]. In Munsell terms it reads 0.3PB 8.5/3.5: high lightness, low chroma, the palest of the institutional blues in our library [2].

The nearest named colors on file are [[uranian-blue]], [[pale-aqua]], [[light-blue]] and [[pastel-blue]], at 3.1, 3.6, [[sky-blue|Sky Blue]] and [[cornflower|Cornflower]] are deeper, more saturated relatives in the same blue family [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a close match to this blue in 64 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.27 percent, and in 39 by the stricter within-painting measure, which makes it rarer than 53 percent of the named colors we track [3]. Inside those paintings it most often reads as a light, 46 percent of the 39, the pale patch rather than an accent or a shadow [3]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 1.9 times the expected rate, and also shows a smaller peak in the 1860s, in 5 of 926 paintings, at 2.2 times expected [3].

The earliest match in our archive dates to 1480, with the latest dated match from 1947, 48 paintings in all, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. That earliest match is 432 years before the name's own earliest record in our sources, 1912: a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a use of this named color [2][3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[3].
